subject: QuiverPay checkout failures — timeline, credit eligibility, and postmortem request
thread_summary: Customer reports intermittent checkout timeouts and high tail latency during afternoon peak leading to failed transactions. Requesting confirmation of impacted window, eligibility for a pro-rata credit, and an RCA/postmortem. Internal engineering pulled traces and provided a timeline and next steps for remediation and evidence handoff.
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@quiverpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failures during 15:00-15:20 PDT — we saw ~2% failed transactions

Hi Irene,

We had a spike of checkout failures this afternoon between ~15:00 and 15:20 PDT. Our monitoring shows ~2% of transactions returned a 504 or timed out at our frontend; users reported abandoned carts. The errors line up with elevated token-level latencies in your API.

Can you confirm Redwood's observed window and whether this qualifies under the SLA for a pro-rata credit? We need:
- Confirmed outage/impact window in UTC and PDT
- Error classes you see (5xx/timeout/latency spikes)
- Any immediate remediation steps we should take to reduce user impact
- Next steps for a formal postmortem and evidence bundle (trace logs, aggregated tail latency histograms)

Attached: small telemetry snippet we captured from our side. Ticket: HUBSPOT-4321.

We appreciate a quick confirmation — this impacted checkout conversion for a handful of high-value merchants.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, QuiverPay
ops@quiverpay.com
(415) 555-0132

---
Attachment: quiverpay_telemetry_snippet_20261004.txt (text)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@quiverpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:40:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures during 15:00-15:20 PDT — we saw ~2% failed transactions

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the snippet. I've looped in Marcus (runtime) and David (incidents) to pull definitive telemetry. We will:

1) Validate the exact impact window from our ingress and model-serving traces
2) Share error-class breakdown (504/502/timeout) and tail-latency percentiles for the window
3) Provide a timeline and a raw trace bundle for your compliance team
4) State our position on SLA credit eligibility and next steps for a formal postmortem

We'll aim to get an initial confirmation within 60–90 minutes and follow with a fuller package by EOD. For now, can you confirm the affected region (I assume us-west / us-central) and whether you want us to prioritize a warmup/config change on your dedicated pool?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@quiverpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 10:05:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — initial traces attached

Alex / Irene,

I pulled the serving traces and ingress logs for the window you mentioned. Quick summary:
- Impacted window (Redwood observed): 2026-10-04T22:58:00Z — 2026-10-04T23:18:45Z (15:58 — 16:18 PDT)
- Primary symptom: spike in 95/99th token latency leading to request timeouts; we also saw a small number of 502s from an autoscaler event in a subset of shards
- Peak request drop: two brief intervals where request success dropped ~3.1% for quiverpay-specific routes

Attachments included: trace_bundle_quiverpay_20261004.tgz (KV cache snapshots + per-request traces), and a short CSV with percentile latencies. The traces show elevated kernel queueing for a short interval while background model warmups were in flight.

Next steps I recommend:
- We can propose a compensatory credit; will confirm eligibility after aligning with SLO definitions and your contract (Irene / David to adjudicate)
- For immediate mitigation, we can push a configuration to increase burst capacity on your dedicated pool for the next 24 hours (requires your OK)

Attachment notes: the trace bundle contains internal execution counters — if you need a redacted version for procurement/legal, let us know.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: trace_bundle_quiverpay_20261004.tgz (trace bundle, 24MB)
Attachment: quiverpay_latency_percentiles_20261004.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@quiverpay.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 10:47:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — proposed remedy and evidence package

Alex,

Thanks for the report and Marcus's quick pull. Per our SLO language (Section 4.1, customer-dedicated-pool SLA) we consider availability degradations from internal autoscaler churn and kernel-queue-induced token latency as eligible for pro-rata remedies when the impact exceeds the contracted threshold over a rolling 30-day window.

Irene and I will run the eligibility calc against your account's commit and the observed 3.1% peak for the 21-minute window. Preliminary estimate: if the contractual uptime threshold is met/exceeded elsewhere this still likely qualifies for a partial credit in the next billing cycle.

Please complete the attached credit-request-form-QuiverPay.pdf and confirm whether you authorize Redwood to run a redacted bundle for legal review. We'll also schedule a postmortem review (30–45 minute sync) once the evidence packet is agreed. Proposed times: Mon 2026-10-05 14:00 PDT or Tue 2026-10-06 09:00 PDT.

If you want immediate relief we can enable burst capacity for 24 hours to reduce tail risk — let me know and we'll flip it.

— David Kim
Manager, Incident Response, Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene / Marcus / David — that timeline matches what we've seen on our side. We authorize Redwood to run a redacted review and will complete the credit form shortly (sending now).

We'd like the 24-hour burst capacity enabled immediately while you complete the adjudication — please flip it on and confirm when active. Also, scheduling preference: Mon 2026-10-05 14:00 PDT works for our team for the postmortem.

One ask: when you provide the postmortem please include:
- Exact root cause hypothesis (autoscaler vs kernel queueing vs model warmup)
- Any configuration changes you propose to avoid recurrence
- If credit is granted, the calculation basis and how it will appear on the invoice

Appreciate the responsiveness — this is high priority for several of our merchants.

Best,
Alex
Head of Integrations, QuiverPay
